evals.name: activate for existing pipeline chart
evals.prompt: Draw a diagram of the six-stage processing pipeline in this crate for the PR description.
required_outcomes: Recheck the dataflow charter before drawing
Read the program's own wiring to derive nodes and edges
Name the conventions being adopted and ask where they fight the domain
prohibited_outcomes: Hand-author a node or edge list beside the code
Present the palette or shape grammar as settled findings

evals.name: do not activate for speculative design
evals.prompt: We're kicking around ideas for a new ingestion service. Sketch roughly how data might move through it.
required_outcomes: Recognize there is no program to derive from and sketch freely
prohibited_outcomes: Build a generator or apply derive-never-draw to a design that does not exist yet

evals.name: activate for hand-maintained list defect
evals.prompt: The diagram script has a list of stage names at the top that we update whenever we add a stage. Add the new stage to it.
required_outcomes: Name the hand-maintained list as a second source of truth
Derive the stages from the program's declarations instead
prohibited_outcomes: Simply append the new stage to the list

evals.name: activate for unclassified element
evals.prompt: The generator's role table doesn't cover the new stage, so it renders without it. Just make it skip unknown stages so it stops breaking.
required_outcomes: Fail the generator on any unclassified element
Explain that an omitted node is invisible in the output
Treat a stale table entry naming a deleted element as a failure too
prohibited_outcomes: Accept that rendering successfully means the chart is correct

evals.name: activate for key fidelity
evals.prompt: The legend is an HTML table of colored cells; one row says 'lilac = external input'. Good enough?
required_outcomes: Draw the key as a graph using the chart's own node shapes, from the same generator
Show the actual glyph instead of naming its color
prohibited_outcomes: Approximate a shape with table cells
Name a color in words in the key

evals.name: activate for eyeballed inset placement
evals.prompt: I nudged the legend offset a few times until it stopped covering anything. Ship it.
required_outcomes: Replace the eyeballed offset with a computed collision check
Check node boxes and edge splines both
Make the check fail the build rather than warn
prohibited_outcomes: Ship an inset positioned by adjusting a number until it looked right

evals.name: activate for a domain the defaults do not partition
evals.prompt: Our nodes are sources, transforms, and sinks — three kinds, not compute-versus-data. Force them into two?
required_outcomes: Extend or replace the convention for this chart
Record the override and its reason in the charter
prohibited_outcomes: Force the domain into the default partition
Apply an override without recording the reason

evals.name: activate but verify the rendering
evals.prompt: I set the rank separation to tighten the rows but it looks the same. The source is right, so it must be a rendering quirk.
required_outcomes: Confirm the rendered geometry actually changed before believing the source
Treat an unchanged bounding box as proof the setting did not apply
prohibited_outcomes: Conclude the tool is at fault without measuring
